issue.title: No error message if redirect at page load goes to nowhere
issue.body:
This is a followup of #3979.

@btford's fix apparently only checks for non-terminal routes referenced from a link object.

If my main component I have this config:

``` ts
  { path: '/', redirectTo: './grid' },
  { path: './grid/...', component: Grid, as: 'grid' },
```

and in my grid component:

``` ts
  { path: './:id', component: Dialog },
```

I get no exception at the page load, but also no working redirect.

With my limited code knowledge I tried to debug this.
It looks like the code runs through https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/angular2/src/router/route_registry.ts#L151 and from that point on simply returns `null` up to the `navigateByUrl` function of the RootRouter called here: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/angular2/src/router./router.ts#L470).

I would love to contribute a plnkr. But I do not see how I can create one which is using the latest git master version of angular.

The same applies for manual router.navigateXXX calls then of course. Though I am not sure how the error messages should be handeled there. In theory those can have a `.catch()` which could handle this, but currently `
    router.navigateByUrl('/grid').catch(() => console.log('error')).then(() => console.log('ok'));` logs `ok` for me... So the error is silently ignored there too.

issue.title: Router requires redirectTo in Child Components for it's root view
issue.body: **Version:** Alpha 45 **Overview:** When using a component that has child components you have to use redirectTo to let the `[router-link]` work correctly when trying to link to the "root" of a child route. I assumed just using "/" and defining a default component would work but its throwing an error. If I put a "redirectTo" in it works as expected but doesn't make sense to me why this is required. I should be able to define a component for "/" **Example** App has a home and cars main set of routes The Cars route has three child routes (default, list, detail) In app.ts: ``` javascript Cars ``` **Currently works with redirectTo** In cars.ts ``` javascript @RouteConfig([ { path: '/', redirectTo: '/default' }, { path: '/default', as: 'Default', component: CarsDefault }, { path: '/list', as: 'List', component: CarsList }, { path: '/detail', as: 'Detail', component: CarsDetail } ]) ``` Plunker: http://plnkr.co/edit/TF4L6ujxtVua2JXYwr3T?p=preview **What I expected to work** ``` javascript @RouteConfig([ { path: '/', as: 'Default', component: CarsDefault }, { path: '/list', as: 'List', component: CarsList }, { path: '/detail', as: 'Detail', component: CarsDetail } ]) ``` **Throws Error:** `EXCEPTION: Link "["Cars"]" does not resolve to a terminal or async instruction. in [null]` from app component Plunker: http://plnkr.co/edit/6fVwFwDLCW0NSajtG6Bv?p=preview I'm not sure if I'm doing something incorrectly, but to me I should be able to just link to /Cars and load the "/" route as the default, not redirect to a different path.

issue.title: TypeError: Cannot read property 'component' of null
issue.body:
## I'm submitting a... 

[ ] Regression (a behavior that used to work and stopped working in a new release)
[x] Bug report  
[ ] Feature request
[ ] Documentation issue or request
[ ] Support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
## Current behavior We have the following route path: **http://www.test.com/App/12/Customer/Products** where **12** is the contract id of the customer. It's a valid id. Once we pass an id, which does not exist, we show the default id, but then we get the following exception, even tho the app still works and is functional: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16785357/28873361-9f46769c-778d-11e7-82ec-0b72595749f9.png) This happens in `app.component.ts` when navigating with: `this.router.navigate` We do this navigation in the `ngOnInit`, because we need to retrieve the `contractId` of the current logged in user via `http get` and set this id in the router. ## Expected behavior Not to have this error: In: `this.canDeactivateChecks.push(new CanDeactivate(outlet.component, curr));` I also can not identify the origin of the error as it's not showing in the stack.
